Stem library

177 candidates, one curve per tight square. Nothing here is in a vase; this is the catalogue.

How to use it. Every single stem has an S-number; every multiple-stem plant has an SM-number. Both carry their source. Tell the sheet which S- or SM-numbers to promote and they can be moved into flowers.html with their own vases. The curves are drawn at their own scale and orientation; the sheet applies the rotation, the 7 in (or 60 mm) height and the vase placement.

The four groups with numbers are the two existing sources of exact data (generators, Euler), the spiral-turns clothoids, the recovered LAC spines, and four gestures. The named-curve group is there because a loop or a drop can be a stem; the LAC group is there because the soft S is the missing middle.

The fractional LAC series (SM17–SM18). The LAC is one law, κ = C(a+s)p; the recovered plates are points on it. SM17 is the same law at p = 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 and 1, with the same start, initial heading, curvature range 1/640 → 1/80 and 360° turn. The p = 1 member is the recovered S52 spine: generating it from the law matches that spine to less than 0.001 of the chord, so the join is the same curve, not a blend. p = 1/2 is the old p = 0.5; 2/3 and 3/4 are the new points in the gap. SM18 carries the series on into p = 1.5, 2, 3 (S53–S55), with p = 1 shared once. The boundary p = ±0.5 stems are removed from the same-angle multiples (SM5/SM6 lose S39; SM7/SM8 lose S41; SM13/SM14 lose S50; SM15/SM16 lose S51) and from the two spiral fans SM9/SM11 (S50/S51), so the jump that prompted the series is gone from the multiples; the individual reference plates remain in the LAC group.

Equal end spacing (SM19–SM22). The gaps between the free ends are not linear in p. With the SM18 mix they run 114–336 in the S52 frame (CV 30%); a constant Δp is much worse (57–652, CV 83%). A log step pi = 1/4·12i/8 brings the CV to 20%; the simple fractions 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 4/5, 1, 11/8, 2, 3 reach 9.8%. The exact equal-tip-arc series is p = 1/4, 0.366, 0.489, 0.631, 0.806, 1.04, 1.378, 1.926, 3; all eight gaps are 236.3–236.5 (CV 0). Fibonacci-like p values are no better than the current mix (27.6%). Distances are in the S52 frame; the card auto-fit leaves the ratios unchanged.

Integer numerators and 3125 (SM23–SM26). These four cards use p = n / 3125, so n = 3125 is exactly p = 1. The log numerators 781, 1066, …, 9375 give CV 20.3%; the equal-tip numerators 781, 1143, …, 9375 give CV 0 but do not contain 3125 (the nearest is 3250). On a 25 grid, forcing 3125 gives 775, 1150, 1525, 1975, 2525, 3125, 4300, 6025, 9375 (CV 7.7%). On a 5 grid it gives 780, 1070, 1370, 1695, 2070, 2520, 3125, 3830, 4880, 6500, 9375 (CV 2.8%). 3125 can therefore be hit exactly on either grid; the 25 grid is the neater one, the 5 grid the closer one.
